status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 the IRA half of this objective is largely enacted through reconciliation while the IIJA half has not been repealed: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) limits the residential clean energy credit (26 U.S.C. 25D) to expenditures through 2025-12-31 (section 70506), the clean vehicle credit (30D) to vehicles acquired through 2025-09-30 (section 70502), and the clean hydrogen credit (45V) to facilities whose construction begins before 2028-01-01 (section 70511), denies the wind and solar credit (45Y) to facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 whose construction begins after 2026-07-04 (section 70512), repeals the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund (section 60002), and, per a law-firm summary, rescinded unobligated IRA loan funding while creating an Energy Dominance Financing program. Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) paused IRA and IIJA disbursements, and DOE announced on 2025-10-01 the termination of 321 awards supporting 223 projects, estimated at about 7.56 billion dollars in savings. Courts have since ordered reinstatement of 27.6 million dollars in commitments (January 2026) and vacated 11 grant cancellations worth 82.1 million dollars (2026-06-11), and 13 states sued over hydrogen hub cancellations (2026-02-18). The FY2026 Energy and Water act (Division B of Public Law 119-74, approved 2026-01-23) gave the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations no appropriation and, per Holland & Knight, reprogrammed about 5.16 billion dollars in unobligated IIJA funds rather than rescinding them.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 orders agencies to pause disbursement of IRA and IIJA funds pending review, with release subject to review and approval by OMB and the economic policy adviser.

Public Law 119-21 is signed. Per the U.S. Code text as amended: the residential clean energy credit ends for expenditures after 2025-12-31 (section 70506), the clean vehicle credit for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 (section 70502), and the clean hydrogen credit requires construction to begin before 2028-01-01 (section 70511); wind and solar facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 lose the section 45Y credit (section 70512); the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund statute is repealed (section 60002). The law's table of contents also lists rescissions of other IRA funds (Sec. 50402 and Secs. 60003 to 60024) and Energy Dominance Financing (Sec. 50403), which were not read.
timeline.source: U.S. Code via Cornell Legal Information Institute

timeline.event: IRS Notice 2025-42 on beginning-of-construction rules for wind and solar takes effect for construction starting on or after this date; it states the credits end for facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 unless construction began before 2026-07-05 (the notice's issuance date is not shown on the page).

DOE announces it has terminated 321 financial awards supporting 223 projects, with estimated savings of about 7.56 billion dollars, issued by OCED, EERE, GDO, MESC, ARPA-E and Fossil Energy; DOE says a case-by-case financial review found the projects did not adequately serve energy needs or return enough value, notes that 26 percent of the terminated awards were made between Election Day and Inauguration Day, and gives recipients 30 days to appeal. S&P Global reports the two largest awards, 2.2 billion dollars, were for West Coast hydrogen hubs.

The FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations act, Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, approved 2026-01-23 per govinfo), is enacted; its text was not readable. The Business Council for Sustainable Energy reports it funds the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations at zero, and Holland & Knight reports it contains no rescissions and reprograms about 5.164 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds, letting Congress carry the balances over.

California, Washington and other states sue DOE in the Northern District of California over the October 2025 cancellations of hydrogen hub and other awards, arguing the cuts violate separation of powers and that a May 2025 DOE review memorandum is a pretext.

A federal judge in the District of Columbia vacates DOE's cancellation of 11 EERE grants worth 82.1 million dollars (date inferred from an article published 2026-06-12); a January 2026 ruling in a similar case had ordered DOE to reinstate 27.6 million dollars in commitments on equal protection grounds.

uncertainties: The enrolled text of Public Law 119-21 was not read (govinfo's page stops in the first title); credit end dates rest on the amended U.S. Code at Cornell's Legal Information Institute, re-read in this review for 30D and 45Y and earlier for 25D, 45V and 42 U.S.C. 7434, and not for 25C or the carbon sequestration and nuclear credits (the Pierce Atwood alert is the source for the home improvement credit ending 2025-12-31). Facilities that began construction by 2026-07-04 keep the earlier wind and solar rules, and IRS Notice 2025-42 addresses beginning of construction. The Energy Dominance Financing and IRA loan rescission claims rest on a law-firm alert and the law's table of contents. DOE's 2025-10-01 release was read through a fetch summary; the 13-state suit and the January 2026 outcome rest on S&P Global, and the 2026-06-11 ruling (Judge Mehta, D.D.C., per Utility Dive) has no caption or docket number and its date is inferred from an article published 2026-06-12. Utility Dive's description of the January outcome (a settlement versus an order) is inconsistent. Division B of Public Law 119-74 could not be read because govinfo's text ends in Division A, so the FY2026 reprogramming of unobligated IIJA funds rests on Holland & Knight (written before signing). Litigation over the January 2025 funding pause was not researched.
